selected_evidence.requirement: Pre-change baseline state of /tmp and /dev/shm on node1
selected_evidence.summary: Showed /tmp had no dedicated mount (part of root xfs) and /dev/shm was tmpfs missing noexec; no fstab entries present

selected_evidence.requirement: Persistent config change: fstab entries for /tmp and /dev/shm with noexec,nosuid,nodev
selected_evidence.summary: cat /etc/fstab shows new tmpfs lines for /tmp and /dev/shm with defaults,nodev,nosuid,noexec after backing up the original file

selected_evidence.requirement: Live activation of the new mount options
selected_evidence.summary: daemon-reload, remount of /dev/shm, mount of /tmp all succeeded; detected and cleaned a duplicate stacked /tmp mount leaving one clean mount

selected_evidence.requirement: Functional proof that noexec/nosuid/nodev are enforced pre-reboot
selected_evidence.summary: findmnt confirms options on both mounts; executing chmod+x scripts placed in /tmp and /dev/shm both fail with Permission denied (rc=126)

selected_evidence.requirement: node1 healthy baseline and boot identity before restart
selected_evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 434803ac-a01f-4272-ba59-a0cdb0c4dd92 and confirmed /tmp and /dev/shm mounts healthy with correct options prior to reboot
systemctl reboot issued; exec stream closed before completion, consistent with the node going down for restart

selected_evidence.requirement: node1 changed boot identity confirming actual restart
selected_evidence.summary: After polling through connection timeouts, exec succeeded again with new boot_id 52b2d6e3-ac2b-42a4-aec8-78a9f3af0dd1, differing from the pre-restart boot_id, proving a real reboot occurred

selected_evidence.requirement: node1 recovered state: mount hardening persisted across reboot
selected_evidence.summary: Post-reboot findmnt shows /tmp and /dev/shm both still mounted with noexec,nosuid,nodev, and functional test scripts on each again fail to execute (rc=126), proving the hardening survived the restart
